doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Joining Basie in 1933 and 1939
summary: He played in Basie's short-lived first band in Little Rock and rejoined after Moten died, in 1939.

bands.name: Andy Kirk's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Now talk to us about when you first started with Basie.

Well I was with Basie’s first band in 1932 or 33, which was short-lived, and actually he was working with Benny Moten at that time. But Moten was having a lot of problems with getting work. So Basie got a job in I think it was Little Rock, Arkansas. And he came to Little Rock and I was there, and I worked with him there in that band.
How did you meet? How did you audition for him or get that spot?

Well, let’s see I’m trying to think had I been with Andy Kirk? No, I don’t think so. But he needed a tenor, and he wasn’t too well known, you know? And he was glad for me to be with his band. Then I worked with that band. But later then he went back to Benny Moten, Hot Lips Page, all of those guys, they went back with Benny, with Benny Moten. So then when Benny Moten died — oh yeah, Walter Page, I don’t want to leave him out, when Benny died, Basie was the one that took over the band, then he sent and got me to join him again. So and that’s when I went back and worked with him I guess about 12 or 13 years off and on.
And what year was this when you first started with the Basie band?

And the first Basie band was in ‘33, the short-lived one. Then the next one was in ‘39 that I joined, 1939, and that was after he was famous. He was famous then in 1939 when I joined. Then I went and stayed about ten, twelve years.
